reflections.title: "The Spirit of the Lord Is on Me"

reflect.text: When Jesus began his public ministry, the Holy Spirit rested upon him in power. The Spirit anointed him to announce good news and bring freedom to broken people. Just as the Spirit equipped Jesus and later filled the church at Pentecost, God gives his Spirit to help us do his work. We make a mistake when we try to serve in our own strength instead of seeking the Spirit's help by faith.

Jesus was sent to set captives free, and real spiritual liberty comes from him alone. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "Christ speaks it by his power, but he bought it by his blood." Jesus took on our bonds and died in our place. He asks for no payment or merit from us, but offers this complete freedom as a free gift.

When Jesus sets us free from the curse of sin, those chains can never bind us again. Satan and our own sinful hearts may still harass us, but God will carry his good work through to the end. Because our bonds have been broken forever, we are free to spend our lives serving God with thankful joy.

questions: Do you rely on the Holy Spirit's help when serving God, or do you try to work in your own strength?
How can you express thankfulness to Jesus today for setting you free from the power of sin?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank you for paying the price on the cross to release us from our spiritual chains. Please fill us with your Holy Spirit so that we do not attempt your work in our own power. Help us to live in your freedom and serve you gladly each day. Amen.

reflections.title: A Prophet Without Honor

reflect.text: Jesus set an example for us by regularly attending the synagogue on the Sabbath to worship God. When he stood up to read the scroll of Isaiah, he declared that the ancient promises of the Messiah were coming true through him. In this moment, he pointed clearly to the work of the triune God, the Father, the Spirit, and the Son.

Nazareth was a small town where people knew Jesus and his family as ordinary, working-class neighbors. Because he lacked formal rabbinic training, his hometown friends stumbled over his humble background instead of recognizing God's hand in his teaching. Their offended pride quickly turned into violent rage, leading them to try to throw him off a cliff, though he walked away unharmed.

Their rejection shows that persistent unbelief does not come from a lack of facts, but from a hard heart that only God's grace can change. When we are overly familiar with spiritual things, we risk missing the truth right in front of us. Rather than being swept away by changeable human feelings, we must check what we hear by studying Scripture every day.

questions: Has familiarity with the Bible or church ever led you to overlook the wonder of who Jesus is?
How can you make a daily habit of testing your feelings and thoughts against God's Word?
reflections.prayer: Father in heaven, soften our hearts so that pride and familiarity never blind us to the truth of Christ. Protect us from being guided by sudden emotions, and anchor us in the teaching of your Word. Grant us your grace to receive your Son with humble faith. Amen.
